options.B: Fear of retaliation or shame often prevents them from telling the truth
options.C: Patients with chronic illness rarely remember how they get hurt
options.D: They want to test the clinical diagnostic skills of the nurse

explanation: Spot on. Fear of making things worse at home or feeling embarrassed makes many victims hide what really happened.

question: Why do certain smells instantly trigger strong memories or emotions?

options.A: Smell signals pass through the visual cortex first
options.B: The nose shares a direct blood supply with the hippocampus
options.C: Odorants directly stimulate the motor strip in the frontal lobe
options.D: Olfactory pathways connect directly to the limbic system in the brain

explanation: You got it! Unlike other senses, smell signals bypass the brain's relay station (the thalamus) and go straight to emotional centers like the amygdala and hippocampus. That's why a scent can instantly remind you of home!

question: How would you simply describe what stress is to a patient?

options.A: A vitamin deficiency caused by poor dietary habits
options.B: A rare psychological disorder requiring lifelong medication
options.C: The body's reaction to demands that disrupt normal balance
options.D: An infectious disease spread through community contact

explanation: Think of stress as your body's natural alarm system kicking in when pressures get too heavy and knock you off balance. You've got this!

question: When introducing a new practice to a unit, why is it so helpful to involve local peer champions?

options.A: Peer champions are the only staff members legally allowed to train others
options.B: Local champions work longer hours without extra pay than regular nurses
options.C: Staff trust and follow respected colleagues more readily than distant managers
options.D: Hospital policy requires a peer champion to sign off on every patient chart

explanation: As student nurses, we know we look up to our senior colleagues and trusted peers for guidance. Peer influence is a powerful tool for positive change!

question: What is the primary goal of inhalation therapy?

options.A: To deliver medication directly to the respiratory tract
options.B: To remove excess fluid directly from the pleural space
options.C: To bypass the digestive system completely for nutrition
options.D: To increase blood pressure through systemic absorption

explanation: Inhalation therapy deposits drugs straight into the airways and lungs for a localized effect. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h1)

question: What is the main sign of ICT (Information and Communication Technology) addiction?

options.A: A temporary fascination with video games during school holidays
options.B: The physical inability to learn how to operate a personal computer
options.C: An allergic reaction to electromagnetic radiation from screens
options.D: Compulsive use of digital devices that interferes with daily life

explanation: You've got this! ICT addiction happens when device use gets out of hand, starting to affect your schoolwork, daily tasks, and relationships.

question: What factor most heavily influences how well a newborn with a birth defect will recover?

options.A: The baby's birth weight alone
options.B: How severe the defect is and how fast treatment starts
options.C: Which hospital branch they were delivered in
options.D: The time of day the baby was born

explanation: Catching things early and getting fast medical or surgical help makes all the difference in a baby's long-term health.

question: Why should a nurse avoid crushing an enteric-coated tablet?

options.A: It turns the solid pill into an unmixable powder
options.B: It changes the color of the liquid mixture
options.C: It causes the medication to dissolve too slowly
options.D: It ruins the special coating designed to protect the stomach

explanation: Enteric coatings protect the stomach lining from irritation or protect the drug from stomach acid; crushing destroys this barrier. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T14#GNS122_U1_T14_h1)

question: What must be done to heat-sensitive instruments after they undergo chemical cold sterilization?

options.A: Store them immediately inside a sealed plastic bag
options.B: Wipe them dry with an ordinary cloth towel
options.C: Rinse them thoroughly using sterile water
options.D: Heat them briefly over an open spirit flame

explanation: Chemical sterilants are toxic to human tissue and must be washed off with sterile water to prevent chemical burns or irritation. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T68#GNS214_U1_T68_h3)

question: Why do healthcare workers count out loud before doing a lift together?

options.A: It helps everyone lift together at the exact same moment
options.B: It distracts the patient from feeling any pain
options.C: It signals visitors to leave the room quietly
options.D: It measures the exact seconds the transfer takes

explanation: Teamwork makes the dream work! Counting down ensures everyone pulls or lifts in unison so nobody drops the weight.

question: Which animal is the main definitive host for the Echinococcus tapeworm?

options.A: Human
options.B: Dog
options.C: Sheep
options.D: Cow

explanation: Dogs and other carnivores carry the adult tapeworm in their guts and pass out the eggs in their stool.

question: Which of these is NOT a non-motor function linked to the cerebellum?

options.A: Language and word retrieval
options.B: Emotional mood modulation
options.C: Primary visual perception
options.D: Working memory and planning

explanation: Primary vision is handled in the occipital lobe at the back of the brain, not the cerebellum (though the cerebellum helps track eye movements!). You're crushing these questions.

question: What happens during the implementation stage of a health plan?

options.A: The health committee writes down initial budget guesses
options.B: All nurses retire and hand over duties to administrators
options.C: The community is surveyed to see if they want a clinic
options.D: The planned health programs and services are put into action

explanation: Implementation is the active phase where your written plans finally turn into real care for people.

question: How do effective unit managers keep patients safe during tough staff and resource shortages?

options.A: By charging patients exorbitant fees for basic cotton wool
options.B: By pretending that the shortages do not exist at all
options.C: By turning away every single patient who walks through the door
options.D: By using creative resourcefulness and strong advocacy skills

explanation: Brilliant! Even when resources are tight, resourceful managers find safe workarounds and fight hard for what their ward needs.

question: What is the main goal of primary health care in our communities?

options.A: Disease prevention and health promotion
options.B: Providing specialized hospital care
options.C: Advanced surgical interventions
options.D: Exclusively managing chronic illnesses

explanation: Spot on! Primary health care is all about stopping sickness before it starts and keeping people well, rather than waiting for them to need major hospital procedures. [learn more](GNS124_U2_T6#GNS124_U2_T6_h1)

question: A patient with Lassa fever spent 10 minutes talking face-to-face with a colleague inside a small office without a mask. How should we view this colleague?

options.A: Casual contact needing no follow-up
options.B: Index case requiring immediate hospital admission
options.C: Close contact requiring active monitoring
options.D: Recovered immune person needing a booster shot

explanation: That's right! Sitting face-to-face in a small room without a mask for 10 minutes is high-risk exposure, so we treat them as a close contact.

question: Which organ system takes over the final excretion of fetal nitrogenous wastes once they cross the placental membrane?

options.A: Fetal kidneys
options.B: Fetal liver
options.C: Maternal lungs
options.D: Maternal kidneys

explanation: Once urea and creatinine diffuse into the mother's blood, her kidneys filter them out and excrete them in her urine. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T7#GNS121_U6_T7_h6)

question: Why do nurse researchers like using histograms for patient data?

options.A: To replace the need for ethical board approval in clinical trials
options.B: To quickly visualize the distribution and spread of a data set
options.C: To prove a causal relationship between two separate nursing interventions
options.D: To track the exact medical record number of every patient in a study

explanation: Turning raw numbers into a clear picture helps you spot patterns and averages at a glance. Simple and super helpful in research!

question: Which two medications belong to the Class IV calcium channel blocker group?

options.A: Lidocaine and flecainide
options.B: Digoxin and adenosine
options.C: Verapamil and diltiazem
options.D: Metoprolol and atenolol

explanation: Verapamil and diltiazem are non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers used to control heart rates in SVTs. [learn more](GNS223_U1_T3#GNS223_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why do many lung cancer patients only discover they are sick when the disease is already advanced?

options.A: The lungs lack pain receptors, allowing tumors to grow undetected initially.
options.B: Symptoms only appear after the cancer completely destroys the heart.
options.C: Early lung tumors cause immediate total paralysis of the limbs.
options.D: Blood tests detect the cancer cells only during late stages.

explanation: You got it! Because lung tissue doesn't have pain nerve endings, a small tumor can grow quietly for a long time without causing any physical pain.

question: What is the main goal of primary health care (PHC) services in Nigeria?

options.A: Handling complex surgical procedures for urban residents
options.B: Conducting advanced medical research in laboratories
options.C: Training international medical specialists
options.D: Bringing essential health services close to the grassroots

explanation: You've got this! Primary health care is all about bringing basic, friendly health services right down to the local communities where everyday people live.

question: When should the nurse document the findings and actions of a home visit?

options.A: Only when the client complains to the hospital
options.B: At the end of the month during salary review
options.C: Immediately after returning from the visit
options.D: Whenever the supervisor remembers to ask for it

explanation: Prompt documentation ensures details are fresh and accurate, preventing errors in the client's medical record. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T6#GNS314_U4_T6_h7)

question: A patient who just had lung surgery is scared to cough because their incision hurts. What should you, the nurse, do first?

options.A: Tell the patient that coughing is optional and let them sleep all day.
options.B: Apply a tight chest binder to completely immobilize the chest wall.
options.C: Administer prescribed pain medication before encouraging controlled coughing exercises.
options.D: Report the patient immediately to the surgeon for emergency re-operation.

explanation: Wonderful clinical judgment! Controlling the pain first allows the patient to cough and clear their lungs safely without agony, preventing complications like collapsed lung areas.

question: What is the main benefit of writing accurate notes during family planning follow-ups?

options.A: Ensuring safe continuity of care when different providers see the client
options.B: Advertising new clinic services to the community
options.C: Providing a colorful drawing book for pediatric visitors
options.D: Reducing the physical weight of clinic filing cabinets

explanation: Clear notes mean that if another nurse or doctor sees the client next time, they can easily pick up right where you left off.

question: What happens during the McRoberts maneuver when dealing with shoulder dystocia?

options.A: The mother's thighs are flexed sharply toward her abdomen
options.B: The mother is turned completely onto her hands and knees
options.C: Firm pressure is applied directly on top of the mother's fundus
options.D: The nurse pulls gently on the baby's head to release the shoulder

explanation: Pulling her knees right up to her chest changes the pelvis angle and helps pop that stuck shoulder free without pulling on the baby.

question: During a surgical scrub, why must you keep your hands higher than your elbows at all times?

options.A: To easily reach the wall soap dispenser
options.B: To follow theatre posture rules
options.C: To let more oxygen flow into your arm muscles
options.D: To stop dirty water and soap from running back down onto your clean hands

explanation: Gravity is always pulling down! Keeping hands high ensures dirty water runs away from your clean fingers.

question: Which clinical finding shows up early in a measles infection?

options.A: Yellow discoloration of the eye sclera
options.B: Painful spasms of the jaw muscles
options.C: Koplik spots inside the oral cavity
options.D: A thick grey membrane in the throat

explanation: Spot on! Koplik spots look like tiny grains of salt on a red background inside the cheeks, and they are a dead giveaway for early measles.

question: What does health equity mean?

options.A: Doctors and nurses earn the same monthly salary
options.B: Every hospital receives the exact same amount of money
options.C: All patients pay identical fees for prescriptions
options.D: Everyone gets resources based on their specific needs

explanation: Equity focuses on fairness and giving extra support to disadvantaged groups to achieve equal health outcomes. [learn more](GST321_U6_T3#GST321_U6_T3_h5)

question: What happens to your pupil when you walk from a dark room into bright sunlight?

options.A: It turns completely white and opaque
options.B: It constricts to let less light enter
options.C: It flattens out against the cornea
options.D: It dilates to capture more light rays

explanation: Your pupil shrinks (constricts) in bright light to protect your eyes from getting overloaded. Easy peasy!

question: How does the cardiovascular center in the medulla help regulate blood pressure?

options.A: By releasing digestive enzymes into the blood
options.B: By producing red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: By adjusting heart rate and blood vessel diameter
options.D: By filtering excess water out of the bloodstream

explanation: The cardiovascular center changes how fast the heart beats and how tightly blood vessels squeeze to keep blood pressure stable. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T21#GNS211_U3_T21_h4)

question: Why are patients with swollen bellies (ascites) told to cut down on salt?

options.A: Salt makes the body hold onto water, worsening fluid in the belly
options.B: Sodium directly destroys liver cells if eaten in large amounts
options.C: Sodium prevents the body from absorbing water pills (diuretics)
options.D: High salt diets instantly trigger severe esophageal bleeding

explanation: Remember the golden rule: water follows salt! Keeping sodium low stops the kidneys from holding onto extra water, easing belly swelling.

question: What is the key difference between Acute Stress Disorder and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder?

options.A: Whether the patient has physical injuries or not
options.B: The time frame and duration of the symptoms
options.C: The age of the person experiencing the trauma
options.D: The specific type of disaster that caused the trauma

explanation: Acute Stress Disorder happens shortly after the event, whereas PTSD involves long-lasting symptoms that persist over months or years. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h3)

question: When assessing a patient's supplement use, which detail is MOST important to record?

options.A: The color and shape of the retail cardboard packaging
options.B: The political affiliation of the supplement manufacturer
options.C: The exact product name, dosage, and frequency of intake
options.D: The name of the transport vehicle used to deliver the pills

explanation: Knowing the exact name and dose helps you and the medical team spot potential drug clashes right away.

question: In the SMART framework for setting goals, what does the letter 'M' stand for?

options.A: Meaningful
options.B: Measurable
options.C: Mandatory
options.D: Managed

explanation: 'M' is for Measurable! It means we include numbers or clear indicators so we can track our progress and see how well we are doing.

question: Why is it correct to say gender roles are social constructs?

options.A: Because they are identical in every country across the world
options.B: Because they depend strictly on the presence of the Y chromosome
options.C: Because they are permanently encoded in human DNA at conception
options.D: Because they are created by human cultures and change across different times and places

explanation: Well done! Because they are human-made rules, gender roles change from culture to culture and shift over time.

question: A nurse is checking a 15-year-old girl who feels very tired, dizzy, and has pale nail beds. What is the best first step to take?

options.A: Test her for color blindness
options.B: Order an immediate full-body MRI scan
options.C: Do a mandatory neurological reflex exam
options.D: Check her BMI growth chart and ask what she usually eats

explanation: You got it! Growth charts and a simple diet history help nurses quickly spot physical growth patterns and nutritional gaps causing that fatigue.

question: Which clinical sign do nurses commonly track to check a patient's nutrition progress over time?

options.A: Steady weight trends
options.B: Eye pupil reactions
options.C: Hair color changes
options.D: Shoe size measurements

explanation: Correct! Tracking weight changes over time gives us a clear picture of whether our nutrition plan is working.

question: When is the best time to document patient care and assessments?

options.A: Before performing the actual physical assessment
options.B: Immediately after the care is provided
options.C: Whenever the head nurse requests a chart review
options.D: At the end of the 12-hour shift from memory

explanation: Always chart right away! Waiting until the end of a long, tiring shift makes it easy to forget important details.

question: A patient comes in with diarrhea, stomach cramps, and fatigue. What is an important question to ask during your nursing assessment?

options.A: Inquiring about recent international air travel to Europe
options.B: Checking the patient's family history of genetic blood disorders
options.C: Reviewing past surgical procedures performed in childhood
options.D: Asking about water sources and sanitation practices at home

explanation: Since tummy troubles and parasites are heavily linked to our surroundings, checking how the patient gets their drinking water and manages waste is a great diagnostic clue.

question: Why do public health nurses rely heavily on epidemiology during a community assessment?

options.A: To design interior floor plans for rural primary health centers
options.B: To calculate the exact daily salary of local healthcare workers
options.C: To measure the distribution and causes of health issues in populations
options.D: To diagnose rare genetic diseases in single family members

explanation: Epidemiology provides the methods to study how diseases spread and who they affect, which helps nurses understand community-wide health patterns. [learn more](GNS124_U3_T4#GNS124_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why must an instrument be thoroughly cleaned before it undergoes disinfection or sterilization?

options.A: Cleaning agents instantly sterilize the instrument without needing an autoclave
options.B: Leftover organic matter and dirt can shield germs from the chemical or heat
options.C: Dry blood makes the metal instruments much heavier to carry
options.D: Patients will complain if the instruments look dull or stained

explanation: Organic debris like blood and tissue acts as a physical barrier that prevents disinfectants and steam from reaching the microorganisms underneath. [learn more](GNS122_U2_T6#GNS122_U2_T6_h2)

question: What is the primary focus of modern occupational health nursing?

options.A: Promoting and protecting worker well-being
options.B: Providing long-term hospital bedside care
options.C: Designing factory machinery and tools
options.D: Managing corporate financial portfolios

explanation: Occupational health nursing centers on safeguarding the health, safety, and overall well-being of employees across various work environments. [learn more](GNS225_U7_T2#GNS225_U7_T2_h1)

question: Which specific weight change should a patient with heart failure report immediately to their healthcare provider?

options.A: Gradually losing one kilogram over a full month
options.B: Staying at the exact same weight for two consecutive weeks
options.C: Gaining more than two kilograms in a couple of days
options.D: Fluctuating by a few grams after eating a large evening meal

explanation: A rapid weight gain over a short period is a reliable sign of fluid retention and worsening heart failure before other symptoms appear. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T13#GNS213_U1_T13_h5)

question: Why is daily movement so important for patients who are stuck on bed rest?

options.A: It cures underlying chronic medical conditions completely
options.B: It prevents the loss of muscle strength and joint flexibility
options.C: It guarantees a shorter hospital stay for every patient
options.D: It eliminates the need for pain medication administration

explanation: Lying in bed all day makes the body weak very quickly. Simple daily movements stop muscles from wasting away and keep joints moving smoothly.

question: Why is keeping a steady level of calcium in your body so important for daily function?

options.A: It prevents the pancreas from producing too much digestive acid.
options.B: It is required for proper nerve conduction and muscle contraction.
options.C: It maintains the normal filtering pressure inside the liver lobules.
options.D: It directly controls the total volume of circulating red blood cells.

explanation: Calcium is essential for sending nerve signals and making your muscles move smoothly. Without it, your nerves and muscles simply cannot function right!

question: What is the big danger if you fail to mix a diluted lotion thoroughly?

options.A: Extending the expiration date by several months
options.B: Turning the entire mixture into a watery liquid
options.C: Creating concentrated hot spots that irritate the skin
options.D: Changing the color of the cream to bright yellow

question: Why should you gently clean and dry the skin before applying a fresh layer of medicated cream?

options.A: To remove old medication residue, sweat, and dirt that could block proper absorption
options.B: To test if the patient's skin is sensitive to water
options.C: To permanently sterilize the skin surface against all bacteria
options.D: To open up the pores so the skin absorbs the entire tube at once

explanation: Cleaning clears away old cream and sweat barriers so the fresh medicine can make direct contact with the skin.

question: Why is 'system interoperability' such a big deal when hospitals share patient records?

options.A: It stops nurses from making any type of documentation error
options.B: It allows different health departments and facilities to share patient data smoothly
options.C: It ensures that all hospitals use the exact same brand of computer hardware
options.D: It prevents patients from viewing their own medical test results online

explanation: Exactly! Interoperability simply means different computer systems can talk to each other, so patient information travels safely between labs, clinics, and hospitals.

question: Why are rats, mice, and insects so dangerous around a kitchen?

options.A: They make food lose its vitamins too quickly
options.B: They make annoying noises that disturb staff and guests
options.C: They eat too much food and increase restaurant bills
options.D: They carry and spread dangerous germs on their bodies and waste

explanation: Pests carry loads of bacteria, viruses, and parasites. When they crawl over surfaces, they leave behind invisible pathogens that can make people sick.

question: Which of these is a very common reason to perform a laparoscopy?

options.A: Extraction of kidney stones
options.B: Drainage of a cerebral abscess
options.C: Repair of a fractured femur bone
options.D: Removal of an inflamed appendix

explanation: Brilliant! Removing an appendix using tiny cuts (laparoscopic appendectomy) is a very common and safe way to treat appendicitis.

question: How does reading professional nursing journals help you find a great research topic?

options.A: It points out existing knowledge gaps and areas needing more study
options.B: It gives exact answers for every single patient diagnosis
options.C: It eliminates the need to ever talk to patients
options.D: It automatically provides funding for hospital equipment

explanation: When you read past studies, the authors usually drop hints at the end about what they didn't get to figure out. That's your cue to step in!

question: As a nurse preparing a discharge plan for a patient recovering from an incomplete abortion, which action directly fulfills the family planning pillar of PAC?

options.A: Discussing and providing the client's preferred modern contraceptive method
options.B: Scheduling a mandatory follow-up appointment for major pelvic surgery
options.C: Handing out educational pamphlets on infant nutrition and immunization
options.D: Referral to social welfare for financial empowerment programs

explanation: Well done! Providing contraceptive services before discharge helps women prevent future unintended pregnancies.

question: What is the main focus of humanistic learning theory?

options.A: Computer-like processing speed and short-term memory limits
options.B: Observing role models in clinical hospital environments
options.C: The whole person, personal growth, and emotional well-being
options.D: Strict behavioral conditioning through rewards and punishments

explanation: Humanism cares about you as a complete human being—your feelings, your dreams, and your personal growth—not just your grades on a score sheet.

question: Which group makes up most of the residents in long-term care facilities?

options.A: Adults admitted strictly for acute post-surgical wound care
options.B: Children with congenital respiratory complications
options.C: Younger adults recovering from short-term sports injuries
options.D: Older adults with multiple chronic illnesses and frailty

explanation: Spot on! Older adults make up the majority of long-term care residents because aging often brings multiple health needs that require daily support.

question: What is a recommended strategy when communicating with an elderly client who has mild hearing loss?

options.A: Direct all your questions to their young family members
options.B: Write everything down and refuse to speak out loud
options.C: Shout at the top of your lungs from across the room
options.D: Speak clearly in a normal tone without shouting

explanation: Shouting distorts sound and can sound aggressive. Speaking clearly at a moderate pitch and facing the client works best for mild hearing loss. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h7)

question: Why is rapid access to patient information critical for nurses at the bedside?

options.A: It replaces the need for verbal patient handovers
options.B: It eliminates the need for physical patient assessments
options.C: It allows nurses to diagnose surgical conditions alone
options.D: It prevents treatment delays and duplicate testing

explanation: Having quick access to past medical history and test results helps nurses avoid repeating tests and speeds up safe care delivery. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h1)

question: When you help a patient improve their nutrition knowledge, what practical skill does it usually help them master?

options.A: Surgical techniques for weight loss
options.B: Hospital administrative policies
options.C: Food labels and portion sizes
options.D: Pharmaceutical drug interactions

explanation: You got it! Boosting health literacy means helping patients decode food packages and understand serving sizes so they can take charge of their plates.

question: Why is keeping clear records of vital signs and treatments especially crucial in flight nursing?

options.A: Insurance companies only pay if notes are written in ink
options.B: It provides a clear record of care despite changing jurisdictions
options.C: Pilots require nursing notes to navigate the aircraft
options.D: It replaces the need for verbal handoffs at the receiving hospital

explanation: You got it! Because air transport often crosses different regions and hospitals, detailed notes ensure smooth handovers and safe, continuous care.

question: The spinothalamic tract is famous for carrying which type of sensory information to the brain?

options.A: Fine touch and vibration
options.B: Conscious motor commands
options.C: Pain and temperature
options.D: Involuntary heart rate signals

explanation: Whenever you touch something hot or feel a sharp pinch, the spinothalamic tract is the main highway rushing that pain and temperature info up to your brain!

question: Which lab result do you expect to see when a patient has acute endometritis?

options.A: High blood glucose level
options.B: Elevated white blood cell count
options.C: Decreased red blood cell count
options.D: Low platelet count

explanation: Since the body is fighting a bacterial invader, the bone marrow pumps out extra white blood cells, leading to a high white blood cell count on the lab report.

question: What do standard Liver Function Tests (LFTs) primarily check in the blood?

options.A: Red blood cell count and hemoglobin levels
options.B: Enzymes and proteins related to the liver
options.C: Electrolytes and kidney filtration rates
options.D: Clotting factors only produced in the bone marrow

explanation: You've got this! LFTs simply look at substances made, processed, or released by the liver to see how well it's doing its job.

question: Which of these is a must-have before launching any new health program in a community?

options.A: Immediate international funding approval
options.B: Completion of the final program evaluation report
options.C: Permanent replacement of all local health staff
options.D: Community readiness and willingness to participate

explanation: If the community isn't ready or interested, even the best health plan won't work. Always get the people on board first!

question: What is the best body position for a patient receiving inhalation therapy?

options.A: Flat on the back with a low pillow
options.B: Lying flat on the left side
options.C: Pronated face down on the bed
options.D: Upright sitting or high Fowler's position

explanation: Sitting upright allows the diaphragm to move freely and promotes maximum lung expansion during medication delivery. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T5#GNS212_U2_T5_h5)

question: What do we call the shift in hospital work when patient needs are way higher than the supplies we have?

options.A: Crisis standards of care
options.B: Standard hospital routine
options.C: Outpatient preventive care
options.D: Elective surgical planning

explanation: You've got this! Crisis standards help healthcare workers ethically and safely ration limited resources when disasters overwhelm the facility.

question: What is the main goal of 'deinstitutionalization' in mental health care?

options.A: Treating patients within local communities to maintain social ties
options.B: Closing all healthcare facilities to rely entirely on home remedies
options.C: Stopping the use of all medications for mental health conditions
options.D: Transferring all psychiatric patients to permanent prison cells

explanation: You got it! Deinstitutionalization simply means moving care out of big, isolated asylums and into local neighborhoods so patients can stay close to their families and support systems.

question: Why do nurses routinely measure head circumference in infants and toddlers during clinic visits?

options.A: To screen for potential neurological or brain development issues
options.B: To check if the child has a normal chest expansion rate
options.C: To calculate the exact caloric intake needed for daily growth
options.D: To determine what shoe size the child will wear as an adult

explanation: Head growth goes hand-in-hand with brain development. Tracking it helps catch issues like fluid buildup in the brain early on.

question: Which type of immunity includes the natural body barriers we are born with, like unbroken skin and stomach acid?

options.A: Passive immunity
options.B: Artificial immunity
options.C: Adaptive immunity
options.D: Innate immunity

explanation: That's right! Innate immunity is your body's built-in, first line of defense that stops pathogens right at the door.

question: Which observable sign in a disaster survivor suggests an immediate need for professional psychological intervention?

options.A: Asking repeatedly when the relief trucks will arrive
options.B: Quietly crying while talking to a family member
options.C: Being completely unresponsive or paralyzed by panic
options.D: Complaining about the taste of the emergency food

explanation: Total unresponsiveness or severe panic indicates that the person's coping mechanisms have completely collapsed. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T6#GNS315_U5_T6_h5)

question: What is the main reason hospitals use standardized usability questionnaires for electronic health records?

options.A: To test the speed of the hospital internet server cables
options.B: To measure user satisfaction and ease of use in a structured way
options.C: To calculate the financial budget for buying new computers
options.D: To check if the computer hardware is physically clean

explanation: Exactly! These questionnaires give hospitals a clear, reliable score on whether their software is actually user-friendly for nurses.

question: Why does the government bother controlling and monitoring health spending?

options.A: To ensure that health workers receive tax exemptions
options.B: To eliminate all private hospitals in the country
options.C: To replace traditional medicine with imported drugs
options.D: To manage limited resources and prevent financial waste

explanation: Money is never unlimited! Governments regulate health spending to make sure public funds are used wisely without unnecessary waste.

question: What is the main idea behind situational leadership?

options.A: Every nurse manager should use an autocratic style
options.B: Only transformational leaders succeed in healthcare
options.C: Leadership style never changes regardless of the task
options.D: Leaders must adapt their style to the context and staff

explanation: Situational leadership requires changing how you lead based on the needs of the staff and the situation at hand. [learn more](GST321_U3_T3#GST321_U3_T3_h6)

question: What is another common medical name for synovial fluid aspiration?

options.A: Arthrocentesis
options.B: Paracentesis
options.C: Thoracentesis
options.D: Lumbar puncture

explanation: Arthrocentesis specifically refers to puncturing a joint space to remove fluid for testing or pain relief. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T8#GNS222_U1_T8_h1)

question: A patient sees a nurse open a pre-used syringe pack but says nothing. What is the main reason for this silence?

options.A: A desire to test the nurse's clinical skills
options.B: Complete understanding of sterilization processes
options.C: A preference for receiving injections over tablets
options.D: Power imbalance and fear of appearing disrespectful

explanation: Spot on! Patients often swallow their worries because they are scared of offending someone they view as superior.

question: Which lifestyle habit should you recommend to a patient trying to manage chronic anxiety?

options.A: Drinking several energy drinks daily to boost energy
options.B: Limiting caffeine intake and establishing regular sleep routines
options.C: Working night shifts to avoid social interaction
options.D: Eliminating all physical exercise from the daily schedule

explanation: Spot on! Caffeine is a stimulant that can mimic or worsen panic, while good sleep helps keep the nervous system balanced and steady.

question: What is the primary driving force for providers in a free market healthcare system?

options.A: State control
options.B: Fixed budgeting
options.C: Equal access
options.D: Financial profit

explanation: In a market-based system, the profit motive encourages private entities to invest, innovate, and compete for patients. [learn more](GST322_U1_T4#GST322_U1_T4_h1)

question: What is the single most effective way to stop infections from spreading between patients in a ward?

options.A: Closing the windows to keep outdoor dust away
options.B: Consistent and proper hand hygiene by all staff
options.C: Burning all hospital bedsheets after a single use
options.D: Using scented air fresheners in the delivery room

explanation: You nailed it! Good hand hygiene is the number one defense against hospital-acquired infections.

question: How does critiquing a qualitative study differ from critiquing a quantitative study?

options.A: Qualitative critique requires complex mathematical formulas to check the P-value
options.B: Qualitative critique ignores the research question completely
options.C: Qualitative critique focuses on data saturation and credibility instead of sample size formulas
options.D: There is no difference in how both types of studies are evaluated

explanation: Because qualitative research explores human experiences using words, evaluators look for depth, meaning, and trustworthiness rather than statistical power. [learn more](GNS224_U4_T4#GNS224_U4_T4_h4)

question: Which principle says that a learning task must match your current level of knowledge?

options.A: Principle of Suitability
options.B: Principle of Adequacy
options.C: Principle of Variety
options.D: Principle of Relevance

explanation: Suitability means the task fits your current stage of learning—not too hard, not too easy. It meets you right where you are!

question: What is the main goal of giving a standard clinical vaccine?

options.A: To provide immediate chemical relief from chronic joint inflammation
options.B: To destroy all existing white blood cells in the patient's body
options.C: To permanently block the liver from metabolizing oral medications
options.D: To introduce safe antigens that stimulate long-term memory cells

explanation: Vaccines give a harmless 'practice preview' of an infection so the immune system can build memory cells and protect the patient later.

question: What is the main purpose of denial when a patient first receives a terminal diagnosis?

options.A: It acts as a protective shield against shocking news
options.B: It stops the physical progression of organ failure
options.C: It proves the patient is uncooperative with staff
options.D: It permanently cures the underlying medical disease

explanation: Denial is a normal psychological buffer that gives the human mind time to slowly accept overwhelming reality. [learn more](GNS321_U4_T16#GNS321_U4_T16_h2)

question: A nurse leading a polio vaccination campaign notices sudden community resistance due to false rumors spread on social media. What is the best immediate response?

options.A: Punish any community member who asks questions about the vaccine
options.B: Engage trusted community leaders to openly address and debunk the rumors
options.C: Ignore the rumors completely and hope the villagers forget them
options.D: Cancel the entire vaccination campaign and close the health clinic

explanation: Rumors spread fast, but trusted local voices spread clarity faster! Partnering with community leaders is the best way to calm fears and protect public health.

question: Why is ensuring a deep latch crucial during early breastfeeding sessions?

options.A: It prevents maternal nipple pain and ensures milk transfer
options.B: It triggers immediate passage of meconium stools
options.C: It stops the baby from swallowing excess air bubbles
options.D: It keeps the baby's body temperature stable

explanation: A deep latch puts the milk ducts in the baby's mouth rather than just the nipple, protecting the mother from damage while getting milk out effectively. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h6)

question: When reviewing literature, what do we call the missing or weakly studied areas in current research?

options.A: Financial grants
options.B: Research gaps
options.C: Patient registries
options.D: Nursing licenses

explanation: Spotting what is missing in current studies points directly to research gaps that need investigation. Great job thinking like a researcher!

question: Which mental health challenges show up most often in physical rehabilitation wards?

options.A: Obsessive-compulsive disorder and phobias
options.B: Depression and anxiety
options.C: Schizophrenia and bipolar disorder
options.D: Dementia and delirium

explanation: Well done! Dealing with sudden lifestyle changes, chronic pain, and loss of independence makes depression and anxiety very common here.

question: Where is the safest spot to drop medicated eye drops into a patient's eye?

options.A: Into the lower conjunctival sac
options.B: Directly onto the cornea
options.C: Into the upper eyelid fold
options.D: In the inner corner of the eye

explanation: Gently pulling down the lower lid creates a nice little pocket (the conjunctival sac). Dropping it here prevents poking the sensitive cornea and keeps the medication right where it's needed.

question: Why do nursing educators often use platforms like Zoom or Google Meet?

options.A: To automatically administer and grade physical injections
options.B: To replace clinical bedside practice with computer games
options.C: To track the exact physical location of nursing students on duty
options.D: To hold virtual classes, webinars, and multidisciplinary huddles

explanation: These video platforms allow educators to connect with large groups of students or staff for lectures, training, and team meetings. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T5#GNS113_U3_T5_h4)

question: What does an endemic disease mean in a community?

options.A: An outbreak that affects only travellers arriving from overseas
options.B: A rare condition that has been completely eradicated by vaccines
options.C: A disease that is constantly present at a predictable baseline level
options.D: A sudden wave of infections that spreads across multiple countries

explanation: An endemic disease maintains a steady, predictable presence within a specific population rather than appearing as a sudden unexpected wave. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T14#GNS313_U1_T14_h1)

question: Which chromosomal change causes Down syndrome?

options.A: Trisomy 13
options.B: Trisomy 21
options.C: Deletion of chromosome 5
options.D: Monosomy X

explanation: Down syndrome is caused by the presence of an extra third copy of chromosome 21. [learn more](GNS111_U1_T7#GNS111_U1_T7_h6)

question: Which patient will benefit most from a nebulizer instead of a standard inhaler?

options.A: An active athlete who needs a quick rescue puff before playing football
options.B: A severely breathless patient who struggles to coordinate breathing with an inhaler
options.C: A healthy adult who prefers taking their daily maintenance medication quickly
options.D: A patient who experiences dry mouth from using anticholinergic inhalers

explanation: Nebulizers turn liquid medicine into a cool mist that the patient can breathe in easily during normal breathing, making them perfect for someone in severe respiratory distress.
